questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:

options.text: Closed.
Greased.
Open.
Removed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: The liquid discharge valves must be open during loading and unloading. They should be closed at all other times.

questions.question: If you are operating a vehicle built before 1998 and are unsure if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Assume the vehicle has ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes. This will tell you if the trailer has ABS.

questions.question: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:

options.text: To ensure safety.
To maximize gas mileage.
To wake up before the drive.
To fill up time.

questions.correctAnswerText: To ensure safety.
questions.explanation: Vehicle inspections before every trip protect you and others on the road. State and federal laws require these safety inspections.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Wheels should be chocked.
The engine should be running.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wheels should be chocked.
questions.explanation: Before opening the engine compartment, engage the parking brake and chock the wheels. Always check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used, as they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.
Be checked regularly.
Be checked regularly, but only if it is cloudy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to be aware of what is around you at all times.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to vacate the lane closest to an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to vacate the lane closest to an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, move to a different lane if safe to do so. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What can rust around the wheel nuts indicate?

options.text: That the nuts are loose.
That the nuts are wet.
That the nuts need to be replaced.
That the nuts are the wrong size.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts is a sign that they may be loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic while driving a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for your vehicle.
Let other drivers wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Always make sure there is a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported:

options.text: By any driver with a CDL.
By any driver, as long as the total weight of the hazardous materials are under 50 pounds.
By any driver in a rural area.
By a driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: By a driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: When checking a tank vehicle, it is most important to verify that:

options.text: There are no leaks.
There is no frost on the windshield.
The paint is not cracking.
The tires are new.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no leaks.
questions.explanation: The most important thing to check on a tank vehicle is that there are no leaks. Check your vehicle's manual for a complete list of all inspection items.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help drivers see a wider area.
They are illegal to use in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have convex mirrors. Convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What must a driver keep in the vehicle when transporting chlorine?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved
An approved gas mask
A chemical suit
Instructions for emergency workers

questions.correctAnswerText: An approved gas mask
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: When should parking brakes be tested?

options.text: They should not be tested.
They should be tested only after driving a distance.
They should be tested before driving.
They should be tested on a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be tested before driving.
questions.explanation: Always check parking brakes before driving as part of your pre-trip inspection. If the parking brakes do not hold, the vehicle needs to be repaired.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Remove the safety latch.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are secured around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: How should a pre-trip inspection be done?

options.text: It should never be done the same way twice.
It should always be done in the same order.
It should only be done on sunny days.
It should not be done if the vehicle seems to be in good condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Always complete a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure nothing gets skipped.

questions.question: How should brakes be used to control surge?

options.text: They should not be used.
They should not be released too quickly after stopping.
They should be used hard and then released.
They should be used with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not be released too quickly after stopping.
questions.explanation: To reduce surge in tank vehicles when stopping, keep steady brake pressure. Do not release the brakes too quickly after you stop.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Close the service line valve.
Remove the service line valve.
Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the service line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows wheels to lock up.
It stops wheels from locking up.
It makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.
It helps brake lights work better.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up during hard braking.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Stay in the driver's lane.
Try to race the driver.
Ignore the driver's gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver's gestures.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact, do not go faster, and do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: What is important to know when transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages.
The packages must be carried in the cab.
The packages must be loaded on their side.
You cannot use bridges.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around radioactive packages and passes through to nearby packages. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept the shipment
Accept the shipment under protest
Accept the shipment and make a note on the paperwork
Refuse the shipment

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse the shipment
questions.explanation: Carriers must refuse shipments of hazardous materials that are not properly prepared.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what should you expect?

options.text: It will probably stay green as you approach.
It is likely broken.
It will likely change to yellow soon.
It will skip yellow and change directly to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will likely change to yellow soon.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will probably turn yellow before you reach it. Start slowing down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When does an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi
When you experience a trailer jackknife
When wheels regain traction after a skid
When air pressure is above 45 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Why should mirrors show both the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road might make the driver feel sick
Seeing part of the truck gives you a reference point
It is illegal to show only the road in mirrors
You need to see reflections of surrounding vehicles on the trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of the truck gives you a reference point
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Avoid quick changes
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front
Speed up
Avoid using tricks like flashing lights to help others pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up
questions.explanation: If tailgated, increase your following distance, avoid quick moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up will only make it more dangerous by keeping the tailgater close at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is outage when loading a tank?

options.text: Extra cargo
Space for liquids to expand
Space for additional fuel
A place for luggage and personal items

questions.correctAnswerText: Space for liquids to expand
questions.explanation: Liquids expand when heated. A tank carrying liquid needs extra space for this expansion. This extra space is called outage.

questions.question: How can you check if a road is becoming icy?

options.text: Guess
Open the window and check the front of the mirror for ice
Look closely at the road
Check a weather forecast

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and check the front of the mirror for ice
questions.explanation: If you think the road might be becoming icy, open the window and feel the front of the mirror, mirror support, or antenna for ice. If ice has formed there, the road is likely becoming icy too.

questions.question: How can you help prevent a rollover?

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the rig
Keep cargo centered on the rig
Move cargo to the right side of the rig
Keep cargo as far from the ground as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the rig
questions.explanation: A rollover is more likely if cargo is unevenly loaded. Keep the load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature gauge do?

options.text: Not change from its starting position
Gradually rise to the normal operating range
Jump quickly to the normal operating range
Flash until it reaches the normal operating range

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually rise to the normal operating range
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: What is the purpose of multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly
To provide extra gears
To improve gas mileage
To make a vehicle quieter

questions.correctAnswerText: To provide extra gears
questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears. They are usually controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.
